# Scripted sequences — the opening, the lessons, the ending

<!-- Generated by tools/dialogue.py. Edit the prose under the
### headings and nothing else, then run:  python3 tools/dialogue.py import -->

**How to edit this file**

- Change only the text underneath a `###` heading. That text is what the game
  says.
- Leave the `##` headings, the `<!-- key: ... -->` comments and the `###`
  field names alone. They are how the text finds its way home.
- Keep any `%s` and `%d` exactly as they are. The game fills them in with a
  name or a level, and a line that loses one will break.
- Blank lines inside a passage are kept. Leading and trailing ones are not.
- Speaker names are part of the line ("Elder: Good morning."). The dialogue
  box splits them off itself, so keep the `Name: ` prefix.

## The opening: the prologue and the well

<!-- key: script:scripts/world/game_opening.gd -->

<sub>game/scripts/world/game_opening.gd</sub>

Each entry below is one page or line, shown in this order.

### PROLOGUE_SPEAKER

THE ELDER

### STARTER_JOINED_TEXT

%s joined you!

### ASK

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Find him, hear what he has seen, and do as he tells you, in the order he tells you. The altar will still be there at the end of it. Will you go?

### PROLOGUE[0]

Ah, there you are. Sit a moment, and let an old man tell it the way it was told to him. Every child of this town hears it once. You are hearing it the day it becomes yours.

### PROLOGUE[1]

This is the Verdant Reach. Green hills, old roads, and more wild creatures than there are stars over the lake.

### PROLOGUE[2]

Some of those creatures choose to walk beside a person. The two swear an oath to one another, and from that day the creature is Oathbound, and the one who walks with it an Oathkeeper.

### PROLOGUE[3]

Most oaths are quiet ones. Farmers plough with their Oathbound, healers mend with them, children grow up beside them. Ours has never been quiet.

### PROLOGUE[4]

We are not the village we look like. We are what is left of the Guardian Order, and we have kept one watch and no other since before the road had a name.

### PROLOGUE[5]

North of the gate, at the end of that road, there is an altar. A whole kingdom is sealed inside it. Its king, its knights, its walls, folded down into stone.

### PROLOGUE[6]

That king had a son, and the son died, and the king would not have it.

He reached for a magic no crown was ever meant to touch. It brought the boy back wrong, and it took the kingdom with him, and every knight who had sworn to him besides.

### PROLOGUE[7]

Our Order sealed all of it away rather than let it walk.

We have kept that seal ever since. It thins. It always thins, and the dead king stirs under it, and the town sends one of its own up the road to put him back down.

It has been done more times than we have names for. It will be done again after you.

### PROLOGUE[8]

The bells beneath the altar rang last night. Come. I will be waiting for you by the well in the square.

### WELCOME[0]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

There you are. Look at you, standing by the old well. I remember when you could barely see over its rim.

### WELCOME[1]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

You have come of age, and of everything you could have been, you chose the watch your parents kept, and theirs before them. The Order has a new Oathkeeper today.

### WELCOME[2]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

But an Oathkeeper needs a partner. This one hatched in my hearth three winters ago, and it has been waiting for someone worth following.

### STARTER_EXPLAINED[0]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

An Emberling. There is a coal in its belly that never goes out. Fire bites hard against green growing things and against rot, but earth and water will smother it, so choose your fights.

### STARTER_EXPLAINED[1]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Out past the walls it walks beside you and fights for you. Press F and it strikes whatever stands in front of you. Catch a wild creature off guard and you may win before it can fight back.

### STARTER_EXPLAINED[2]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

And take these five Binding Scrolls. Weaken a wild creature in battle, then offer it a scroll. If it accepts, it swears to you as your Emberling has.

### THREAT[0]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Now the part you have known since you were small. The bells beneath the altar rang on their own last night. The seal is thinning, and the dead king is turning over in it.

### THREAT[1]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

So we do what this town has always done. The rite is gathered, the road is cleared, and one of ours walks up to the altar and puts him back to sleep. This turn it falls to you.

### THREAT[2]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

You will not go straight up, mind. Nobody does. Our scout keeps the camp past the north gate, and he keeps the rite with it. Everything the altar needs, he will start you on.

### REPLIES[0]

I'll find him.

### REPLIES[1]

Do I have a choice?

### REPLIES[2]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Good. Follow the road north through the gate, and come back to tell me what he says.

### REPLIES[3]

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Ha! You always have a choice. You simply never pick the other one. North through the gate, then, and come back to tell me what he says.

### REPLIES[0]

I'll find him.

### REPLIES[1]

Do I have a choice?

### AMBUSH_HIT_TEXT

The wild Emberling scorches %s before you can react!

### WON_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

That's the way of it. Come back to the fire.

### LOST_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Easy. I patched you all up. Talk to me when you want to try again.

### CALL_BACK_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Your healer is in the paddock. Press Tab, call it back out, then talk to me.

### NO_HEALER_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

None of yours can heal. Remember this, then: a healer can mend a benched partner. Swap the hurt one out, mend it, swap it back.

### AMBUSH[0]

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Right. First thing a mender teaches you is that—

### AMBUSH[1]

## Lesson: striking first

<!-- key: script:scripts/world/field_strike.gd -->

<sub>game/scripts/world/field_strike.gd</sub>

Each entry below is one page or line, shown in this order.

### PROMPT

Press F to strike the %s before it knows you are there.

### OPENING_TEXT

Your blow landed before the fight began, so %s takes this turn whatever the Loambuck would have done with it.

### LESSON_BANNER

You swung first out in the grass, so this turn is yours: a strike buys the first move, not just the damage.

### WON_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

That's the trick. Come back to the fire.

### LOST_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Never mind the fight. You landed the hit, and that was the lesson. Come back to the fire.

### SIGHTING[0]

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Wait. There's a Loambuck in the grass...

### SIGHTING[1]

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

It hasn't seen you. Press F to hit it first.

## Lesson: being caught in the open

<!-- key: script:scripts/world/field_ambush.gd -->

<sub>game/scripts/world/field_ambush.gd</sub>

Each entry below is one page or line, shown in this order.

### PROMPT

Hold still. Let it reach you and land the first blow.

### OPENING_TEXT

It reached you before the fight began, so it takes this turn and %s answers after it.

### LESSON_BANNER

It swung first out in the grass, so the first move here is its own. That is what standing still costs: the same thing your own strike buys.

### WON_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Good. Now you know both sides: hit first, or don't be there when it swings. Back to the fire.

### LOST_LINE

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Easy. That's what a free hit costs. Come back to the fire.

### CHARGE[0]

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Stay exactly where you are.

### CHARGE[1]

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

An Emberling, and it's seen you. Watch it wind up, then let it hit you.
